_about: Audited and reviewed financial statements of frontier labs, as filed (AI Economy → Models & Labs, src/tabs/ai/LabEconomics.jsx). USD millions. 'quarters' is the filing's quarterly statement of operations, which groups costs by what was bought (compute, people, sales, other); 'periods' adds its by-function table (cost of revenue against research and development) and cash flows, which the filing gives only for years and half-years. Nothing here is estimated: a figure the filing does not give is left out, and anything computed from two filed figures is computed on the page and labelled. Add a lab when it files; add a quarter when an amendment or a 10-Q gives one.

quarters.label: Q2 2026
quarters.sbcNote: First-half stock compensation of $2,185M less the first quarter's $924M; the quarterly table rounds it to $1.3 billion

labs.netLossNote: Net loss is dominated by non-cash changes in the fair value of convertible notes as the company's valuation rose ($59.6B in Q2 2026 alone); operating income is the figure that describes the business.
labs.costOfRevenueNote: The filing says substantially all of cost of revenue is compute and infrastructure for customer-serving workloads, plus some personnel and overhead; research and development is mostly compute for model development. So total compute less cost of revenue is a slight understatement of the compute spent on research and training.
facts: Compute is bought 12 to 18 months ahead, so its cost is fixed in the near term and does not move with demand: revenue growth, not cost cuts, produced the swing to operating profit.
Customers paying $100,000 or more a year grew from about 400 (March 2025) to more than 6,000 (June 2026) and were 74% of first-half 2026 revenue.
Of the $15.1B rise in first-half revenue, $12.1B was consumption-based (the API and usage plans) and $3.0B subscriptions.
